full_judgment: 15. We have already stated above that Annexure-A does not reflect fulfillment of the requirements of section 93(2). The statements of facts made therein shows that the bank balance, purchase of share by investment and bank interest on certain balance and purchase of land by the petitioners have not been shown in the petitioners returns. As such the allegation of escaping assessment and evasion of tax has been made therein. But in the second paragraph of the said notice it has been stated that the wealth statement submitted by the petitioners does not contain anything about the aforesaid wealth. From the statement made in the first and second paragraph of Annexure-A it appears that certain facts are available in the hands of the authority, which relates to nondisclosure of certain wealth and some investments made in the wealth statement submitted by the petitioner. But the language of Annexure-A does not show that the same can be taken as definite information in the possession of the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes specifically when it is stated that “ উক্ত গোপনকৃত সম্পদের উপর প্রযোজ্য আযকর ফাঁকি দিয়াছেন প্রতীয়মান হইতেছে” meaning 'it appears' to the authority that the petitioners have evaded paying tax on the aforesaid wealth which has escaped assessment. From the above statement incorporated in Annexure-'A' it can at best be construed that the Deputy Commissioner might have some information derived from the wealth statement, which of course not assessable, as no income has been claimed from the said wealth. But the said information does not mean that those are definite and sufficient materials in possession of the authority for issuing notice under section 93 of the Ordinance. However, since some information or if the same is treated to be materials, are within the notice of the DCT, the authority must have been cautious in using the words in the notice specifically when the files of the assesses have been closed earlier upon proper scrutiny and examination. Again by using the words প্রতীয়মান হইতেছে it cannot be construed that the DCT has in his possession any definite information/materials from which he could definitely come to a conclusion that the petitioners have evaded paying tax which can be a reason for issuance of such notice for such evasion, if any. Moreover, when the DCT used the term "প্রতীয়মান হইতেছে" meaning "appears to be" in the 1st paragraph of the impugned notice, Annexure A, it cannot be said that definite information was in possession of the DCT. The materials, as appears in Annexure-A, regarding non disclosure of wealth and thereby alleging "escaped assessment", cannot be deemed to be a definite information. Although an assessee, who concealed the particulars of his income or deliberately furnished inaccurate statements in his return, should be dealt with in accordance with law. But fact remains presumption or suspicion never be the basis of or be construed as definite information in possession of the DCT and, as such, cannot be a ground to re-open the file, under section 93. To initiate or to proceed with the case under section 93 facts necessary must be objective, not subjective ones. It is very clear that if any information has any reason to belief that the assessee has escaped assessment and thereby evaded payment of tax then the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes is required to have an honest and reasonable material in his possession upon which such allegation can be based on reasonable ground and is not to be based on mere suspicion, gossip or rumor specifically when the file has been closed after due scrutiny by the DCT on an earlier occasion to his satisfaction. In the present case such definite information appears to be absent specially when the authority used the words "প্রতীয়মান হইতেছে" in Annexure-A which can never be said that the information’s are "definite information" in nature and sufficient materials is in his possession.
